description: NYXARA NOVA  is a team passionate about technology, ethical hacking, cybersecurity, software development, and space exploration. We aim to combine innovation, creativity, and scientific research to solve real-world challenges using technology and NASA data. We welcome curious, motivated, and talented people who want to learn, collaborate, and build impactful solutions.
summary: ASTRA VITAL is an offline-first web application that helps astronauts on long-duration missions monitor their own health when real-time support from Earth is limited. Crew members log key indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, sleep, exercise, fatigue, mood and glucose). A transparent, rule-based engine compares each value with published reference ranges and with the astronaut's own baseline, detects trends, missing data and inconsistent entries, and explains every alert: what changed, why it matters, what to do and when to contact the flight surgeon. Each indicator is linked to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight (RIDGE) through an interactive body map and a Mission Risk Center. Records are stored on the device first and synchronized in batches when a communication window opens, with conflict control and recovery after link drops. We also explored real NASA OSDR laboratory data from the Inspiration4 crew (OSD-575, OSD-569). It matters because, on the way to Mars, astronauts will carry much of the responsibility for noticing health changes early. Educational prototype - not a medical device.
details:
THE PROBLEM
On long-duration missions, astronauts are exposed to space radiation, isolation and confinement, altered gravity, a hostile closed environment and growing distance from Earth. These hazards can affect the cardiovascular system, bone and muscle, sleep, behavior and immune function. With communication delays and limited onboard medical capability, the crew must notice and act on health changes themselves.

OUR SOLUTION
ASTRA VITAL is a working, offline-first health monitoring web application. Astronauts log measurements, see their status at a glance (Nominal / Follow-up / Priority, always shown with color + icon + text), understand why a value matters, and know what to do and when to involve the flight surgeon.

IMPLEMENTED FEATURES (all working in the public app)
- Mission Dashboard: overall status, latest value and sparkline for each indicator, active alerts, mission day, mission environment and signal delay, time since last Earth contact, sync queue, and a daily health routine with streaks and points (gamification) that prompts measurements.
- Log Measurement: validated form with unit, timestamp, data source and notes, plus "how to measure" guidance per indicator. Indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, body temperature, sleep duration, exercise minutes, fatigue (Samn-Perelli scale), mood check-in and blood glucose. Values are entered manually by the crew member; the prototype does not connect to sensors.
- Interactive Body: clickable cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, nervous/behavioral, immune and general systems, colored by status, each with indicators, personal baseline, trend chart, related hazards and a plain-language explanation.
- Health Intelligence Engine: transparent rule-based logic (no machine-learning model) with five rules: (1) data quality (implausible or inconsistent entries are rejected), (2) missing data and gaps, (3) documented reference ranges (AHA, 2017 ACC/AHA, WHO, CDC, AASM/SRS, ADA), (4) deviation of 2 or more standard deviations from the astronaut's own baseline, (5) 7-day trend. Findings for the same indicator are consolidated into one alert. Every alert shows: what changed, the indicator, why it matters, a conservative suggested action, when to contact the medical team, and the rule and source used.
- Mission Risk Center: NASA's five hazards (Radiation, Isolation and confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity fields, Hostile/closed environments) with related risks, the indicators that track them, documented preventive measures and honest limitations. Environment selector: space station, deep-space spacecraft, Moon base, Mars base, rover.
- NASA Data view: real Inspiration4 laboratory values from NASA OSDR compared with the lab reference range of each sample, including data-quality flags.
- Offline-first sync: every record is saved locally first and queued. When a communication window is simulated (AOS), records move in batches of 5 to a ground store and leave the queue only after confirmation; records are versioned, conflicts are logged instead of overwritten, and an injected link drop is recovered at the next window.
- Ground Console: a flight-surgeon view that only sees data actually synchronized and can send notes delivered to the crew at the next sync.
- Earth Medical Reports: printable report (PDF via the browser), HTML report, CSV export, JSON backup and restore.
WHAT IS REAL, WHAT IS SIMULATED
- Demonstration vital signs: SYNTHETIC. The demo crew member is fictional and the scenario (declining sleep, rising fatigue and heart rate, sustained stage-1 blood pressure, one low SpO2 reading, a missed day, a typing error) is generated by a seeded algorithm. It is labeled "synthetic" everywhere in the app.
- Manually entered measurements: anything a user logs in the form is stored and analyzed exactly like real data.
- NASA research data: real, unmodified pre-flight and post-flight clinical laboratory values (OSD-575, OSD-569) from 4 civilian crew members of a 3-day mission. They are NOT continuous in-flight vital signs, and with n = 4 we make no causal claims.
- Earth link and ground synchronization: SIMULATED inside the browser between two local data stores. No real ground server, spacecraft or medical system is connected.

HOW IT WORKS (ARCHITECTURE)
A single self-contained static web page (HTML5, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, inline SVG charts) with no external libraries or network calls, so it keeps working offline once loaded. Data is kept in browser local storage. The health engine (src/engine.js) is pure, deterministic and covered by unit tests; build.py inlines everything into one file deployed on GitHub Pages.

VALIDATION
10 unit tests of the engine and 27 end-to-end checks in headless Chrome (all views, form validation, persistence after reload, sync blocked during loss of signal, recovery after link drop, ground note round-trip, exports, body map interaction, mobile and tablet layouts, zero console errors). The deployed page was verified to be byte-identical to the repository build. No clinical validation has been performed.

TECHNOLOGIES
HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, SVG; Node.js (unit tests); Python, Playwright and Google Chrome (end-to-end tests and screen recording); FFmpeg (video); NASA OSDR public API (data download); GitHub Pages (hosting).

LINKS
Application: https://etner249.github.io/astra-vital/
Source code and documentation: https://github.com/Etner249/astra-vital
Official 30-second demo: https://youtu.be/lxITVao2RmQ
Extended presentation (1:47): https://youtu.be/sz9qzXasEKc

LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE WORK
ASTRA VITAL is an educational prototype, not a certified medical device; it does not diagnose and does not replace flight surgeons or official protocols. Thresholds marked "engine convention" (2 SD, 7-day window, 36 h without data) are engineering choices that need clinical validation. Future work: integration with certified medical devices and wearables, a delay-tolerant ground server, multi-crew views, multilingual interface, and evaluation with flight surgeons and analog missions.

TEAM NYXARA NOVA (Trujillo, Peru) - WE CONTROL THE UNSEEN.
Etner Therry Rios Vasquez (team owner): coordination, architecture, product decisions and presentation. Jeanfranco Alfredo Ibarra Kocfú: technical implementation support and testing. Darlin Saldaña Pinedo: scientific research and documentation. Máximo Fabrizzio Espinoza Peche: testing, validation and presentation.

AI DISCLOSURE
We used an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) to accelerate coding, tests, documentation and video assembly; the idea, scope and decisions are the team's. No AI model runs inside ASTRA VITAL. The video narration is an AI-generated voice (Kokoro TTS) and the team emblem shown in the extended video is AI-generated; both are labeled on screen and in the video metadata and descriptions. ASTRA VITAL is an independent project and is not developed, endorsed or validated by NASA.
